title: From Keser to Abba and Ima: the mazalos, the arms and netzach and hod of Arich Anpin
overview:
Having finished the *Keser*, the chapter shows how *chachma* and *bina*, *Abba* and *Ima*, receive from *Arich Anpin*, in three ways from highest to lowest. *Chachma* is the abstract point, an *ayin*, and *bina* the concrete explanation it shines into; behind the flash is the *koach hamaskil*.

Highest is the way of the *mazalos*, the beard: hairs in the membrane over the brain that drip its liquid, the first six as pleasure and the last six as intellect, *Abba* from the eighth and *Ima* from the thirteenth. The liquid is only leftovers, yet the hair is rooted in the skull, above the brain, like a sealed wineskin that leaks, or the nonsense of a mind under pressure, or the Torah as *novlos* of the wisdom above. So the thirteen attributes of mercy reach the sinner, and everything, even the Torah's sense, depends on the *mazal*. Lower, the intellect garbs the arms, the *middos* of the will, mountains of darkness: it rationalizes a bias like one bribed. Lowest, from *netzach* and *hod*, it is the everyday intellect on autopilot.

sections.title: From Keser into Abba and Ima: three ways the intellect receives from Arich Anpin
sections.summary: Having finished the *Keser*, the chapter turns to the details of *Atzilus*: how *chachma* and *bina* (*Abba* and *Ima*) receive from *Arich Anpin*. There are three ways: from its *Nehi*, from its arms (*chesed* and *gevura*), and from its *mazalos*, the eighth and the thirteenth.

phrases.he: (כה) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין עשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: Now we have to understand the details of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text:
"So today we're going to learn about the beard."

Now that the *Keser* (crown) has been explained, the chapter explains how the *Keser* connects to *chachma* and *bina* (wisdom and understanding), how it is their source. Chapters 1 and 2 explained *Chabad*, and here he starts explaining *Chabad* again. He kind of skips over it, but he explains how it goes from *Arich Anpin* (lit. the long countenance) to *Abba*, to *Abba* and *Ima* (lit. father and mother; *chachma* and *bina* as *partzufim*). So in this chapter there are three ways that the *sechel* (intellect) receives from the *Keser*. Now that the *Keser* of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) has been explained, it is time to explain the details of *Atzilus* itself: the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בירידת האור מחיצוניות נה''י דאריך אנפין באבא ואמא
phrases.en: That is, the way that the light from the *chitzoniyus* of *Nehi* of *Arich Anpin*, from the lowest level of *Arich Anpin*, descends into *Abba*, into *chachma* and *bina*, the *partzufim* of *chachma* and *bina*.

blocks.text:
That is, the way the light from the *chitzoniyus* (outer side) of *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*), the lowest level of *Arich Anpin*, descends into *Abba* and *Ima*, the *partzufim* of *chachma* and *bina*.

There are three ways this can happen. This is the first: the light goes from the *Keser* down through the *Chabad* of *Atik* and *Arich*, to their *Chagas* (*chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*), until the *Nehi*, and the *Nehi* of *Arich* goes into *Abba*. "That's one way."

phrases.en: But sometimes we say

phrases.he: דאבא ואמא מלבישים לזרועות דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: that *Abba* and *Ima* garb, that they clothe the arms of *Arich Anpin*.
And that it says
the head of the king is fixed or dressed up in *chesed* and *gevura*:

phrases.he: היינו בחינת רישא דאריך אנפין דאתתקן בחסד וגבורה דעתיק יומין
phrases.en: that's talking about the way that the head of *Arich Anpin* connects to *chesed* and *gevura* of *Atik Yomin*.

phrases.he: חסד דעתיק יומין בגולגלתא כו' כנזכר לעיל)

blocks.text: But sometimes it says that the *sechel* does not receive from the *Nehi* of *Arich Anpin*. Rather, *Abba* and *Ima* garb the arms of *Arich Anpin*. The right arm goes into *chachma*, the left arm goes into *bina*, and *chachma* and *bina* are like puppets, with the arms of *Arich Anpin* inside them. The arms are the *middos* (emotional attributes) of *chesed* and *gevura* (kindness and might), that is, *Chagas*; so this second way, the *sechel* receives from *Chagas*.

Then a little parenthesis, to say that another teaching of the *Zohar* is not talking about this. The *Zohar* says *reisha d'malka b'chesed u'gevura istakan*, the head of the king is fixed, or dressed up, in *chesed* and *gevura*. That does not mean the *sechel* garbing the arms. It is talking about how the head of *Arich Anpin* connects to the *chesed* and *gevura* of *Atik Yomin* (lit. the Ancient of Days). That is a higher thing, and it was discussed earlier, about the *Keser*: chapter 21 explained how the *chesed* of *Atik Yomin* becomes the *sechel*, and the *gevura* of *Atik Yomin* becomes the *mocha stima'a* (the hidden brain). "So now we're going to say the third way."

phrases.he: ולפעמים אומר דאבא יונק ממזל הח' ונוצר,
phrases.en: Sometimes we say that *Abba* and *Ima*, the *sechel*, receive from the *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*: that *Abba* receives from the eighth *mazal*, which is *v'notzer*,
and *Ima*, *bina*, receives from the thirteenth *mazal*, which is *v'nakeh*.

blocks.text: And sometimes it says that *Abba* and *Ima*, the *sechel*, receive from the *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin* (lit. flows; what they are will be explained): *Abba* from the eighth *mazal*, *v'notzer*, and *Ima*, *bina*, from the thirteenth *mazal*, *v'nakeh*. These thirteen *mazalos* correspond to the *yud-gimmel middos harachamim*, the thirteen attributes of mercy, and that too will be explained.

sections.title: Chachma is ayin, bina is yesh: the flash and the koach hamaskil behind it
sections.summary: *Chachma* is the *koach MaH*, an abstract point grasped without understanding it, and *bina* is the concrete explanation it shines into: from nothing to something. The flash of *chachma* comes from the *koach hamaskil*, the hidden *chachma* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: אך הנה ידוע בענין כח מה,
phrases.en: It's known about the idea of *koach MaH*, the power of what,
that *chachma* comes out from nothing, that the source of *chachma* is that it's an *ayin*.
And *bina* is called a *yesh*.

blocks.text: It is known about the *koach MaH* (the power of what) that *chachma* comes out from nothing, that its source is an *ayin* (nothing). The *koach MaH* is the power to connect to something abstract: the *bittul* (self-nullification) of *ma*, "what". That is *chachma*: you can think about something you do not really understand yet and say, "What is it?" You just know it is there, but you do not know anything about it, and you are wondering about it. That is *koach MaH* in the simplest sense.

So *chachma* is in a way of an *ayin*, and *bina* is called a *yesh* (something). *Bina* is already when you understand something in a tangible, concrete way. You can explain it, and so it is called a something, a *yesh*.

phrases.he: והאור ושפע דאין דחכמה מאיר ונמשך בבחינת השגה דבינה
phrases.en: And so this abstract point of *chachma*, this abstract understanding of the intangible point of an idea, shines into the understanding of *bina*.
That's the idea of going from an *ayin*, from a nothing, to *yesh*, to something; going from something abstract to something concrete.

blocks.text: The abstract point of *chachma*, the intangible point of an idea, shines into the understanding of *bina*. Your *chachma* grasps the intangible part, which is beyond the explanation, and then the explanation holds it. So when you have the explanation, you get more than the explanation itself: the explanation anchors your perception of the abstract point in *chachma*.

blocks.title: The stick figure
blocks.text:
That is why somebody who gets it, and knows what you are talking about, will get what you are saying, and somebody who does not know will not.

It is like a symbol, a stick figure of a person. It is meant only to symbolize a person; it does not actually look like one, only in a very little way. But if you know what the original looks like, when you see the stick figure your mind will conjure up the actual thing. That is one of the meanings of *chachma* being enclothed in *bina*: the explanation is just a kind of symbol that does not carry over the whole idea, but the idea shines into it.

So first of all the explanation is according to the idea, and then in its words you can see that point. But the basic idea is that *chachma* is the abstract point, which shines into the understanding of *bina*, and *bina* explains it and makes it a concrete explanation. That is **from an ayin, from a nothing, to yesh, to something**: from the abstract to the concrete.

phrases.he: ונקרא תרין רעין דלא מתפרשין כו',
phrases.en: And *chachma* and *bina* are called two friends that never part; they always work together.
And they dwell together.

blocks.text: *Chachma* and *bina* are called *trein re'in d'lo misparshin*, two friends that never part, and *k'chada sharyan*, they dwell together. They are always working together: you cannot have a *chachma* without a *bina*, and you cannot have a *bina* without a *chachma*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת נקודה דחכמה שמבריק כברק מלמעלה מן השכל
phrases.en: And this is the idea of the flash of *chachma*: when you get an idea and a light bulb goes on over your head, and all of a sudden you get this idea, like a lightning bolt flashes in your mind.
And this is what the world calls understanding.

blocks.text: This is the flash of *chachma*. You get an idea, a light bulb goes on over your head, all of a sudden it is there like a lightning bolt flashing in your mind: that is the point of *chachma* coming out. Then, from that point, you start right away to develop the idea, to analyze it and figure it out, and that is *bina*.

And this is what the world calls understanding, when people say, "Oh, now I understand." They do not mean that they can explain it, which is what this book would call understanding, because *bina* is only when you understand a thing with all the explanations and have analyzed it. But tell somebody a new idea and they catch the point and go, "Oh": it just flashed in their mind, and that is really a *chachma*. That is what they call understanding, "Yeah, I understand." They cannot necessarily explain it to somebody else; they did not even explain it to themselves. They just saw the point, a little perception of it.

phrases.en: This comes from the *koach hamaskil*, the mind's power to bring out ideas, which is called the power of intellect.
And this is also called the *chachma stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*.
It's also called the hidden *chachma*,

phrases.he: שהוא מקור מוצא כל שכל מאין כו',
phrases.en: and this is the source that brings out every intellect; the idea is brought out from nothing.
And it's called *maskil*, the one that makes the intellect, the intellectualizer.

blocks.text: This lightning bolt of inspiration, this perception of a new idea, comes from the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight), the mind's power to bring out ideas. In *sefiros* it is called the *chachma stima'a* (the hidden wisdom) of *Arich Anpin*, and also *chachma ne'elama*, the hidden *chachma*. It is the source that brings out every intellect: the idea is brought out from nothing, from this source. And it is called *maskil*, the one that makes the intellect, "the intellectualizer."

sections.title: The mazalos: hairs in the brain's membrane that drip the source of pleasure and intellect
sections.summary: The thirteen *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*, the tufts of its beard, are channels through the membrane over the brain: the first six bring pleasure, the last six intellect. *Abba* suckles from the eighth, *v'notzer*, a thin tube, and *Ima* from the thirteenth, *v'nakeh*; the two are united in their source, so study in *bina* brings new flashes of *chachma*.

phrases.he: והיינו שאמר דאור אבא יונק ממזל הח', ונוצר
phrases.en: That *Abba*, *chachma*, suckles from the eighth *mazal*, which is *v'notzer*,
which is the letters of *tzinor*, like a pipe,
because it's like a thin tube.
And so this is the way of the hairs of this eighth *mazal*:

phrases.he: הוא בחינת צומח שבמשכיל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: this is the power of growth from this source of the intellect.

blocks.text: That is what it means that *Abba*, *chachma*, suckles from the eighth *mazal*, *v'notzer*. *V'notzer* has the letters of *tzinor*, a pipe, because it is like a thin tube. And the hairs of this eighth *mazal* are the power of growth in that source of the intellect, the *maskil*.

What he is explaining here is called the beard of *Arich Anpin*, and it corresponds to the actual beard. But it explains it like this. There is the brain, and there is the skull, and between the brain and the skull there is a membrane, called the *kruma d'avira*, the membrane of air. This spongy membrane is full of a liquid, and the liquid drips through tiny hairs in the membrane into the brain. That liquid is the source of intellect: it is, it says, the essential pleasure, and it is also the essential power of intellect.

So when it comes onto the brain, it is revealed as pleasure or as intellect, depending on where it comes out. The thirteen *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin* are like thirteen sections, thirteen ways this liquid comes out through the membrane onto the brain. The first six are on the side of *chesed*: a lot of the liquid comes out there, and when it comes out in abundance it causes pleasure. The last six are on the side of *gevura*, and they are the source of *sechel*, of intellect, because there it comes out in a much smaller way, and so it comes out as intellect.

It starts with the first *mazal*, which comes out in the most abundant form and gives the most general pleasure. As it goes down through the six that correspond to pleasure, it gets more and more localized, until it becomes a very specific pleasure, a *taanug murkav*, a pleasure from a very specific thing. By the time it gets to the last six, it is already intellect.

Of those last six, eight through thirteen, the first, the eighth, is the source of *chachma*. It says the brain of *chachma* is cold and wet, because it has more of this liquid, and that is why it gives a more intuitive, holistic understanding. *Bina*, it says, is dry and hot, because there is very little of the liquid and it comes through very, very thin hairs. It comes in a very localized way, which gives rise to a very specific intellect.

The middle *mazal*, the seventh, *v'emes*, is the intermediary between these two sides. It makes the *hachra'a* (the decision) between *chesed* and *gevura*, so that there is not just an objective intellect but a decision, a choice.

The word *mazal* means like *nozel*, to drip. "I don't know if it's the same source, but in English, like a nozzle": a pipe or a tube. That is the idea. The reason the constellations and the stars are called *mazalos* is that they are channels that bring different things to us. The sun is a channel that brings us heat and warmth and light, and all the different stars and planets are channels that affect the Earth in different ways. A *mazal* is just a channel.

So the *mazalos* of *Arich* are the channels that bring this liquid into the brain, the channels that bring out the pleasure and the intellect. The eighth *mazal*, *v'notzer*, is the source of *chachma*: it is like a *tzinor dak*, a thin tube. The hairs of this *mazal*, its tubes, are what grow the intellect: when the liquid comes out, it develops the idea. That is the brain from which comes the hidden *maskil*, which brings out new ideas, like a *chachma*, an idea that comes out as if from nowhere. That is when it first drips down, and then it grows more and more as it continues.

phrases.en: And this is the idea that it grows, it sprouts from nowhere, from nothing, all sorts of ideas.

phrases.he: והיניקה הוא בחינת הגדלת מוחין דאבא
phrases.en: And that the brain of *chachma* draws life, that it sucks from this *mazal*, is what causes the brain of *chachma* to develop and mature.

phrases.he: והגדלת מוחין דאימא, היינו ממזל הי''ג, ונקה
phrases.en: And the development of the brain of *Ima*, of *bina*, is from the thirteenth *mazal*, which is *v'nakeh*.

blocks.text: It sprouts from nowhere, from nothing, all sorts of ideas. And the suckling, the brain of *chachma* drawing life from this *mazal*, is what makes the brain of *chachma* develop and mature. As it gets more and more of the liquid it develops that particular idea, and in general the whole brain develops and becomes smarter and more mature. And the development of the brain of *Ima*, *bina*, is from the thirteenth *mazal*, *v'nakeh*.

phrases.he: וב' מזלות הללו, מזל העליון ומזל התחתון,
phrases.en: And these two *mazalos*, the highest and the lowest *mazal*,
they are the source for the intellect of *Abba* and *Ima*, of *chachma* and *bina*.
And this source is in the *koach hamaskil* itself.
So in this itself is a source for the development of the brain of understanding, which is, in the language of the world, *chachma*: just to get an idea.
And there's also the source for the development of the brain of grasp, to understand in a way that you can explain it, which is *bina*.

phrases.he: שהן נקראים מוח אבא ומוח אימא כידוע
phrases.en: These two brains are called the brain of *Abba*, the brain of the father, and the brain of the mother, *chachma* and *bina*, as is known.

blocks.text: These two *mazalos* are called the highest and the lowest because they are the highest and the lowest of the ones that relate to *sechel*. They are of the last six; the first seven do not relate to *sechel*. So the highest and lowest of these last six are the roots of the intellect of *Abba* and *Ima*, of *chachma* and *bina*.

And this root is in the *koach hamaskil* itself. In the liquid and the membrane over the brain, in the shape and the way the membrane is constructed, there is a source for your talents and for your intellect. The six that relate to pleasure affect your talents: what you will enjoy, and what you will have aptitude and sensitivity for. The ones that relate to intellect determine how your brain will work and what you will be good at intellectually.

Within this source itself there is a root for developing the brain of understanding, which, in the language of the world, is *chachma*, just getting an idea; and a root for developing the brain of grasp, understanding in a way that you can explain it, which is *bina*. These two brains are called the brain of *Abba*, the father, and the brain of *Ima*, the mother: *chachma* and *bina*, as is known.

phrases.he: וכמו שבחינת מוח בינה שהוא מוח התפיסא וההשגה, מקבל מבחינת האין דמוח החכמה,
phrases.en: And just like in the revealed intellect, first you have an intuitive understanding in *chachma*, a holistic, abstract understanding of *chachma*, and then that understanding is developed and explained by the brain of *bina*,
so too in their source,

phrases.he: ביחוד ב' מזלות דאריך אנפין ונוצר ונקה כו'
phrases.en: with the unification of these two *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*, the *mazal* of *v'notzer* and the *mazal* of *v'nakeh*.

blocks.text: In the revealed intellect, first you have an intuitive, holistic, abstract understanding in *chachma*, and then the brain of *bina* develops and explains it. So too in the source: the intellect starts in the *mazal* of *chachma* and spreads from there to the *mazal* of *bina*. With the union of these two *mazalos* of *Arich Anpin*, *v'notzer* and *v'nakeh*, the source of *chachma* and *bina*, the intellect goes from *v'notzer* to *v'nakeh*. That is why in the revealed intellect the source is *chachma*, which comes from *v'notzer*, and from there it goes over to *bina*, which is *v'nakeh*.

This is also one of the reasons why, when you do *hisbonenus* (contemplation) and study something in *bina*, you get new ideas in *chachma*, new flashes of an idea: in their source, *chachma* and *bina* are connected. When you are active in your brain of *bina*, you draw more liquid into *bina* and activate the *mazal* of *v'nakeh*, and that automatically starts to draw more liquid into *v'notzer* too, which will then bring out a new idea.

blocks.title: What modern science knows about the brain
blocks.text:
As far as what modern medicine and science say about all this, it seems they are still researching the brain, this liquid and the membranes. Rabbi Walters says he has not been able to find anything conclusive about how it works and what its function is. So it is explained here as best as can be from what it says in Torah sources, without trying to make correlations.

In general, correlating what the Torah says with medicine or science is tricky. The terminology is often different, and in modern science there are always new theories, contradictory theories, opinions. Sometimes there is an obvious connection, sometimes possible ones, and sometimes there is just not enough. Maybe in thirty years, or fifteen, or ten, they will research the brain more and figure it out: "we'll have to wait and see." There are something like seventy pages about the brain and its membranes and liquids in the *Zohar*, and he does not know how much modern science really understands the brain. He has heard people say that until now they were researching the liver and the heart and other things, and now they are just starting to really research the brain. "We'll see."

sections.title: Leftovers from a higher source: the hairs, the sealed wineskin and novlos chachma
sections.summary: The hairs carry only the leftovers of the *mocha stima'a*, yet their root is the skull, higher than the brain itself, and that is why they burst out as waste. So too the nonsense that comes out of a mind under pressure, and the Torah, the *novlos* of the wisdom above: a thing forced down low reveals its essence.

phrases.en: And it's known
that even though these *mazalos* are called hairs,
the idea of a hair is that it bursts out of the skin and then it grows out:

phrases.he: רק מבחינת מותרי מוחא סתימאה דאריך אנפין,
phrases.en: they're growing only from the leftovers of the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*.
But their source is from the *atzmus hagulgalta*, from the actual skull itself.

blocks.text: It is known that the *mazalos* are called hairs. They are connected to the hairs of the head and the beard, but here it is talking about the hairs inside the brain, from this membrane; that is the *mashal*, and above it is a certain type of *tzimtzum* (contraction). They are called hairs because a hair bursts out of the skin and then grows out, and they grow only from the leftovers of the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*.

There are two parts of the hair. The hair is like a tube, and the tube itself, inside the brain, is connected to the level of *Keser*, the level of the skull. But the liquid that drips through it is from the liquid called the *mocha stima'a*, the hidden source of the intellect, and what comes through the hairs is only the leftovers of that liquid, a little drop of it. Even so, their source is from the *atzmus hagulgalta*, the actual skull itself.

phrases.en: Which is higher than this liquid.
Therefore
this is the reason why the hairs come out as leftover, or like a waste: because their source is so high.

blocks.text: The skull is higher than this liquid. The liquid represents the source of *chachma*, *chachma* of *Keser*, and the *gulgalta*, the skull, represents *Keser* of *Keser*, which connects to *Atik Yomin*: *Atik* is enclothed in the skull. And that is why the hairs come out as leftover, as waste: because their source is so high. "That's why." What's the *mashal*?

phrases.he: כמשל בקיעת הנוד סתום ביותר כו'
phrases.en: Like if you have a very tightly sealed wine skin or a water sack: if it's very full and very tight, some of it will seep through the pores, it will leak out a little bit.

blocks.title: The tightly sealed wineskin
blocks.text: If you have a very tightly sealed wineskin or water sack, very full and very tight, some of the liquid will seep through the pores and leak out a little bit. So too the brain: because the skull forms a very tight seal, it forces some of the liquid to go through the membrane into the brain. But it is just little drops, leftover. It really mostly stays on top of the brain, and only the pressure forces some of it through.

phrases.he: כמו החכמה כשגובר עליו כח בשכל ביותר,
phrases.en: For example with your intellect: when somebody's really thinking hard, and the power of the intellect is really pressuring it,
so besides coming up with good ideas, they'll also come up with some ridiculous nonsense.

phrases.he: ששרש הנובלות יותר גבוה מגוף אור השכל
phrases.en: But actually the source of these jokes or this nonsense is higher than the intellect itself.

blocks.title: The think tank
blocks.text: You see something like this with the intellect. When somebody is really thinking hard and the power of the intellect is really pressuring it, then besides good ideas they will also come up with some ridiculous nonsense. Take a think tank, where you are working to brainstorm and figure out some idea, really pressing your mind: you come up with a lot of good ideas, and you also come up with a lot of nonsense. That is *novlos*, the leftovers, the waste.

But the source of these jokes, this nonsense, is actually higher than the intellect itself, than what makes sense, because it is connecting to the level that is higher than intellect, and that is forcing the intellect to come down. The fact that it is forced to come down into low things shows it is coming from a higher source; otherwise it would not come down so low. When the intellect comes down into ridiculous things, into nonsense, it shows that it is not just functioning on its regular level but is being pushed by the *Keser*, from higher than the intellect.

That is why *shtus* (foolishness) that is higher than the intellect can come out and look like *shtus*: the idea of *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness). Even in *kelipa*, *shtus* comes from the *ratzon* (will), forcing the intellect to go a certain way, and the intellect will come out with whatever the *ratzon* tells it to, even if it is stupid.

blocks.question: Does this mean that whoever says stupid things is very smart?
blocks.text: No. Just because somebody is saying stupid things does not mean he is very smart; he could just be saying stupid things. What is meant is *sichas chullin shel talmidei chachamim*, the everyday talk of Torah scholars. The jokes of a *talmid chacham* really have deeper wisdom hidden in them than his actual teachings, the Torah he teaches, because the things too deep for him to explain normally come out in a joke. It brings out the *etzem* (essence) of the idea in a different way, a *levush zar* (a strange garment), like a *mashal* or a *chida*, a riddle. If regular people have *shtus*, and it does not come as a result of thinking, that is just because they were not thinking so hard.

He is not talking about a regular joke that is just nonsense. He means that sometimes things seem very low but really come from a high place. In the *Gemara*, for example, there are different stories of how the sages would joke with each other, and there was a very big *chachma* going on there. In this case these low things are actually **higher than the intellect itself**, than the light of the *sechel*.

phrases.he: ולכך אמר דנובלות חכמה של מעלה תורה,
phrases.en: Therefore it says that the Torah is like the leftover waste of the *chachma* above, of G-d's wisdom.
And it says that this is a praise.
Like it's explained elsewhere.

blocks.text: That is why it says that the Torah is *novlos chachma shel maala*, the leftover waste of the wisdom above, G-d's wisdom. And it says that this is *l'shevach davka*, specifically a praise. It is not trying to put the Torah down and say, "Oh, the Torah is like nothing of G-d's wisdom." G-d lowered His wisdom to tell us what to do with our cows, what happens if one cow gores another, how to keep *Shabbos*, how to do your business, how to eat and how to sleep, how to walk and how to dress: all these very low, mundane things. For the intellect that would be *novlos*, a very petty little thing, like garbage.

But the fact that the *sechel* comes down to that shows that the whole purpose of the *chachma* of *Atzilus* and of *Adam Kadmon*, the whole *chachma*, is only for us. It reveals that Hashem's *etzem* chooses us, down here in this world, and that this is the real purpose of the *chachma*, and so it reveals the connection of the *chachma* to the *etzem*. As it is in itself, it is not connected to the *etzem*; it is just *chachma*. But when the *chachma* comes out as Torah, for us to make a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), it reveals Hashem's *etzem* in the *chachma*. That is why the Torah is *davka* the biggest *chachma*, why it is not just a *chachma*: Hashem's *etzem* is there, and that is brought out specifically when it comes down very low.

This is one of the big general rules in *Chassidus*: whenever something on a high level, or relatively higher than something else, is forced to come down to the lower level, in order to go down it has to reveal its *etzem*, which is higher than its level. So when it comes down it actually gains, because it reveals its *etzem*.

That is why, if you want to really understand something, teach it. You will understand it much better than if you just learn it for yourself, because having to lower it down and explain it simply forces you to understand it much deeper.

And if you want to bring it out *l'maaseh*, to live it, or to tell somebody a practical *hora'a* (instruction), not just explaining them a theory but advising what to do, like a *Rav* who has to *pasken* a *halacha*, or a *mashpia* (mentor) who has to give somebody advice, then *davka* there you get to the real *etzem* of the *sechel*, higher even than when you teach it. That is *lilmod al menas laasos*, learning in order to do.

He was just learning *Hemshech Samech Vav*, he says, but this rule is in a lot of *maamarim*, all over the place. There it says that a *Rav* who has to *pasken* is afraid he is going to mess it up, because it is not a theory; he has to tell them the right thing. That fear gives him a deeper *bittul* to the idea than his pleasure in explaining it would, and the deeper *bittul* lets him get to the *etzem* of the idea, which he could not reach with just the enjoyment of it.

That is the advantage of a *Rav*, but it holds even if you are not a *Rav*, even just for yourself: if you learn so that you know what to do in your house, or learn *halacha* to know what to do, or in case somebody asks you and you need to know what to tell them. Even when you learn *Chassidus*, you have to know: so what do I do? What is *Chassidus* telling me to do? How does it tell me to live my life differently than if I would not learn it? And if somebody comes and asks, "How should I act in this situation?" You have to bring out the practical *hora'a* in everything.

This is one of the big rules, which the Rebbe stressed a lot, a *klal* in *Chassidus* and in Torah: everything, even the highest ideas, needs a practical application, a *hora'a l'poel*. At the end of every *sicha* and every *maamar* there is always a *hora'a l'maaseh*, some lesson in our *avoda*, because that is how you get to the *etzem* of the idea, by bringing it out like that. As it is explained elsewhere, about the Torah being *novlos chachma shel maala*.

sections.title: Thirteen attributes of mercy and "everything depends on mazal": the Essence above reason
sections.summary: The thirteen attributes of mercy are the tufts of the beard: they reach the very low, our sins, and so show a connection higher than Torah and reason. So when *Abba* suckles from the *mazal* it receives from the essence of *Keser*, and even the *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*, the union of *chachma* and *bina*, depends on the *mazal*: G-d decides what makes sense.

phrases.he: וכך הוא טעם מעלות ענין שרש י''ג מדות הרחמים
phrases.en: This is also the reason why the thirteen *middos harachamim* are so great,

phrases.he: שנקרא בשם י''ג תיקוני דיקנא כו',
phrases.en: and they're called the thirteen tufts of the beard.
The idea of the beard is that it comes out from the leftovers of the brain.

blocks.text: This is also why the *yud-gimmel middos harachamim* (the thirteen attributes of mercy) are so great. They are called the *yud-gimmel tikunei dikna*, the thirteen tufts of the beard. What is so special about them, and why call them the beard? The beard comes out from the leftovers of the brain, a little bit of an extra thing coming out. But the fact that it comes out to such a low thing shows that its source is very high.

The thirteen attributes of mercy are *davka* for when we sin; they relate to very low things, and that Hashem connects to those low things shows that their source is really higher than the Torah. Hashem is able to forgive us when we do these low things, and even make our *aveiros* (sins) into *mitzvos*, and that shows we have a connection higher than the Torah: an essential connection, higher than a reason, higher than a *sechel*.

phrases.en: Like it says,
*Hashem* passed over His face,
and He said, *Hashem*, *Hashem*.

blocks.text: As it says, *vaya'avor Hashem al panav vayikra Hashem Hashem*. When the thirteen attributes of mercy are said, it says Hashem passed over His face, meaning He went past the *pnimiyus* (the inner side), past the *sechel* and everything, to the *etzem*; and He said, "*Hashem*, *Hashem*," and then He said the thirteen attributes.

phrases.en: It reaches all the way up to the *etzem*, which is higher than the *mocha stima'a*, the source of the intellect,

phrases.he: שנקרא טעם וחכמה כמוסה לרצון הנעלם,
phrases.en: which is the hidden reason and the *chachma* that's in the *ratzon*, which is like the *geshmak*, the pleasure you get out of it.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן שכל הנעלם מכל רעיון
phrases.en: This is also called the *sechel* which is hidden from all thought,
or the wonders of *chachma*.

blocks.text: That means it reaches all the way up to the *etzem*, which is higher than the *mocha stima'a*, the source of the intellect. The *mocha stima'a* is the hidden reason and the *chachma* in the *ratzon*, the *geshmak* (relish), the pleasure you get out of it; but this is higher, the *etzem*'s connection to it.

Hashem has a *bechira* (choice) in the Jews, higher than a reason and everything; there is a level where they are connected to Hashem just because He chose them, and that is higher than the intellect. So even something that does not make sense according to intellect can come out there. Even a person who, according to Torah, sinned, so that you would say he should not be connected to Hashem: Hashem says, "No, we'll forgive him anyway, and we'll connect him anyway."

It is also called *sechel hane'elam mikol ra'ayon*, the *sechel* hidden from all thought, or *pla'os chachma*, the wonders of *chachma*: all of that is the source of the *sechel* in the *Keser*, and this is higher than that.

phrases.en: Based on this,

phrases.he: כשאמר דאור אבא יונק ממזל כו',
phrases.en: when it says that the light of *chachma* receives, it sucks from the *mazal*,

phrases.he: הרי זה למעלה מחכמה סתימאה עצמה

blocks.text: So when it says that the light of *Abba*, *chachma*, sucks from the *mazal*, that is higher than the *mocha stima'a* itself. It does not just mean that it receives the little bit of liquid that drips in, from the *mocha stima'a*, the source of the *chachma*, the *chachma* of *Keser*. That is true. But it even receives from the *etzem* of the *Keser*, which is higher than that, because that is what forces the liquid to come down. So it is really receiving from the *etzem*.

phrases.en: And this is why it says,
everything depends on a *mazal*,
even a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת יחוד אבא ואמא למטה
phrases.en: which is the idea of the union of the *Abba* and *Ima* of *chachma* and *bina* below, your understanding:
the point of *chachma* in the *heichal* of *bina*.

blocks.text: That is why it says *hakol talui b'mazal*, everything depends on a *mazal*, even a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal* (the sanctuary). That is the union of *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*, below: your understanding, the point of *chachma* in the *heichal* of *bina*. So even the understanding of the Torah depends on the *mazal*.

There is more here. Really the source of the *sechel* is in the *etzem*, which is higher, and the *etzem* is what decides what is going to make sense; even the way the *chachma* is going to come out is according to it. The *mitzvos* are really from Hashem's *ratzon*, which is higher than any reason, and Hashem's connection to the Jews is just from His *etzem*, which is higher than a reason. The only reason the Torah makes sense is that Hashem said it should make sense that way. But when you reveal its source in the *mazal*, you reveal the level where it could come out anyway.

This is one of the things *Chassidus* does: it reveals the *etzem* of the *sechel*. That is why in *Chassidus* the same thing is explained in many ways, even opposite ways, and then it shows how they all connect. When you reveal the source in the *etzem*, it takes what in ordinary *sechel* would be ridiculous, stupid, like reading a thing in an opposite way, or reading it in two opposite ways and showing how they connect, and it does that, because that is really the *etzem* of the *sechel*: a much higher *sechel*.

phrases.en: This is *sefer* and *sippur*.
That's called a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*.

blocks.text: This is *sefer* and *sippur*. The Torah is the *sefer* (book), and *bina* is the *sippur* (telling), and both of them are according to the *sofer* (scribe), the one who makes the *sechel*, which is the *etzem*. That is called a *Sefer Torah* in the *heichal*, as is known. At this level the *sechel* is according to the *etzem* and the *bechira*, and so the *sechel* can be made however He wants. Hashem decides what is going to make sense, and because He decided it should make sense, that is why it makes sense. It comes all the way down: Hashem decided that the Torah and *mitzvos* should be a certain way, and that is now the nature of the world.

If you actually went and did a scientific study of the world, you would come to the conclusion that the best thing, *al pi sechel* (according to reason), is to do things according to the Torah. Nevertheless, that is only because Hashem chose that it should be that way.

blocks.title: Why one plus one is two
blocks.text:
"Right, yeah, math only makes sense because G-d said it should make sense." G-d made the world so that one plus one is two, and that is why it makes sense that one plus one is two. If G-d had made the world so that one plus one is three, then it would make sense that one plus one is three, "because He made your fingers that way." It is hard for a person to imagine otherwise, because he lives in this world and does not know anything else.

But even in this world, as was explained, what is the source of one plus one being two? It is an *Echad* (one made of parts united). Only because Hashem made the idea of *Echad* do you have math: it makes sense to us to group separate things together into a unit.

blocks.title: Three apples in a bowl
blocks.text:
If I have three apples in my bowl, I say one apple, two apples, three apples: "Oh, I have three." That it makes sense to count them together is only because Hashem made in the world this idea of seeing separate things as part of a higher unity. If G-d had made the world only with the level of *Kadmon*, we would say, "What do you mean?" We would just have an existential view of the world. The apple is an apple. Just because it is near another apple does not make it two apples. There is one apple and there is one apple; one plus one equals one plus one, that is what it equals, it does not equal two. When you have three, you have one and one and one; you do not have three.

What is the idea of making them into a unit of three, so that they lose their identity, their individuality, and are just a number? It is only because our minds make generalities and see similar things as just another one of the same thing. But they really are not; each one is its own unique thing.

blocks.title: No such thing as apples
blocks.text:
In a way, it does not make sense to count them and say, "Oh, one plus one is two." No, they have nothing to do with each other: this is one, and this is one. What do you mean, "I have ten"? That means they are all the same thing. There are even philosophies that say this: there is no existence of a generality like "apples", only individual apples, each one different. On the level of *Kadmon*, each one is individual and unique and has no connection to a generality; in actuality there is no general thing called apples, only particular, separate things.

A generality is a thing of *Echad*. But Hashem made the world so that our minds should work that way: we make generalities and see a unity that is not a physical thing that is there, but a mental or spiritual thing that unites similar things, even though they are really separate and unique. Because Hashem made us that way, we can count. Otherwise we would not be able to count.

sections.title: The arms of Arich Anpin: the middos of the will, mountains of darkness
sections.summary: Receiving from the *mazalos* is far higher than garbing the arms, *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, and higher still than *Nehi*. The *middos* of the will are called mountains of darkness: like mountains the sun did not raise, they are feelings the intellect could never cause, rooted in the hidden *chachma*, the *ta'am kamus* that splits into *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: וזהו למעלה הרבה ממה שכתוב שאבא ואימא מלבישין לזרועות דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: And this way, where the *sechel* receives from the *mazalos* of *Arich*, is much, much higher than when the *sechel* garbs the *chesed* and *gevura*, the *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, which is what we said is the arms of *Arich Anpin*,

phrases.he: ומכל שכן מבחינת נה''י דאריך אנפין שמלובשין באבא ואמא כו'
phrases.en: and for sure it's higher than when the *sechel* garbs the *Nehi* of *Arich Anpin*.

blocks.text: Three ways are being explained in which *Abba* and *Ima* receive from the *Keser*, from *Arich Anpin*. The first is by way of the *mazalos*, and in this way they receive something of the actual essence of the *Keser*. The hairs are hollow. First, they are tubes that bring in a little of the liquid from the *mocha stima'a*, the *chachma* of *Arich Anpin*, the source of the *sechel*. But the hair itself, not the liquid inside it, reaches all the way up to the skull; its source is in the skull, the actual *Keser* of *Arich*, and there the seven lower *sefiros* of *Atik* shine. So it is the revelation of *Atik* in the *sechel*. This is the level of *Chassidus*, *Atik*'s level, when it shines into the *sechel*: "It's like what we're doing now."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 27 opens by summing up lines 22-31 (the hairs and the mazalos) before it reads line 35.

blocks.text: When it says hairs, it means both literally the hairs of the beard and the head, and what they correspond to, the hairs inside the head, which are hairs "in quotes". As the *Zohar* would say, *is searos v'is searos*: there are hairs, and then there are hairs. The tubes that go from the membrane over the brain into the brain are called hairs, but they are not actually hairs; they are little tubes.
blocks.outOfPlace: Part of class 27's opening summary of lines 22-31, before it reads line 35.

blocks.text: Now the next way it receives from *Arich Anpin*. The way the *sechel* receives from the *mazalos* of *Arich* is much, much higher than when it garbs the *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, its *chesed* and *gevura*, what was called its *zro'os* (arms). And it is surely higher than when the *sechel* garbs the *Nehi* of *Arich Anpin*. So now he explains the level of *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.en: Being that it's known

phrases.he: שבחינת ז׳ תחתונים דאריך אנפין היינו רק בחינת המדות חג''ת כו'
phrases.en: the seven lower *sefiros* of *Arich Anpin*, which are the *middos*, *Chagas* and *Nehim*:

phrases.he: שנקרא יד הגדולה ויד החזקה כו',
phrases.en: those *Chagas*, the *chesed*, *gevura*, *tiferes*, are called the great hand, the strong hand, the uplifted hand.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן בזהר בשם טורי חשוכא
phrases.en: And these *middos* are also called in the *Zohar* the mountains of darkness.

blocks.text:
It is known that the seven lower *sefiros* of *Arich Anpin* are only the *middos*: *chesed*, *gevura*, *tiferes*, *netzach*, *hod*, *yesod* and *Malchus*. The *Chagas*, *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, are called the *yad hagedola*, the great hand, the *yad hachazaka*, the strong hand, and the *yad rama*, the uplifted hand.

They have a *heh* ("the" great, "the" strong) because in *Arich Anpin* this is the source, the highest level that is revealed downward. With the *Keser*, its *chitzoniyus* is revealed and its *pnimiyus* is not, so the highest level that is revealed, an infinite revelation, is the *middos* of *Arich Anpin*. A *mashal* will come soon. And these *middos* are also called in the *Zohar* the *turei chashocha*, the mountains of darkness.

phrases.he: (כידוע במאמר דהאי איילתא אזלת לטורא חשוכא
phrases.en: As it's known about the teaching in the *Zohar* that says this gazelle runs to the mountain of darkness,
and from there it gets its food, it eats the grass there.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת עליית המלכות בחג"ת דאריך אנפין כו'
phrases.en: This is the idea of *Malchus*, which is called the gazelle, going up to receive from the level of *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*.
Like it says, the ark was lifted up, and it rested on Ararat,
in the seventh month, which is *Tishrei*,
and this is the idea of *Rosh Hashana*.

phrases.he: שעולה המלכות בהרי אררט טורי קרדניתא כו')
phrases.en: On *Rosh Hashana*, *Malchus* is lifted up to the mountain of Ararat, which is the mountain of darkness.

blocks.text: As is known from the teaching of the *Zohar*: this gazelle runs to the mountain of darkness, and from there it gets its food; it eats the grass there. That is *Malchus* (kingship), called the gazelle, going up to receive from the *Chagas* of *Arich Anpin*, its *middos*. That is called the gazelle going up to the mountains of darkness, because the *middos* of *Keser* are called the mountains of darkness, as will be explained in a minute.

As it says, the ark was lifted up and rested on Ararat, and the mountain of Ararat is called the mountain of darkness. It rested in the seventh month, *Tishrei*, which is *Rosh Hashana*. It did not actually rest on *Rosh Hashana*; it rested on the seventeenth of the month. But the ark being lifted up to Ararat is what happens on *Rosh Hashana*: *Malchus* is lifted up to the mountains of Ararat, the *turei kardunisa*, the mountain of darkness. That is the level of the *middos* of *Arich Anpin*, and the idea of these *middos* will be explained in a moment.

phrases.he: כמו הרים הגבוהים שאין אור השמש מאיר עליהם כו'
phrases.en: This is like a *mashal* of mountains that are so high that the light of the sun doesn't shine on them.

blocks.title: Mountains the sun could not raise
blocks.text: They are called mountains of darkness after a *mashal* of mountains so high that the light of the sun does not shine on them. What does that mean? There are different ideas: a very high mountain blocks the sun, so a whole side of it is dark; or it is snow-capped because it is not hot up there. But one explanation he saw spelled out in another place in *Chassidus* is this. There are hills and mountains made by the pull of the sun and the moon: besides the tidal effect on the water, they have a certain effect on the earth, and they can pull up the ground, maybe indirectly, and make mountains. But there are certain very high mountains on Earth that would never exist from those forces. They are there only because Hashem specially made the world, from the beginning of creation, to have them. How, he leaves open: either it was just made like that, or maybe tectonic plates are pushing the ground up at that place, and it keeps getting higher and higher, like the Himalayas. These very high mountains are called higher than the sun, meaning beyond the sun's ability to cause.

In the analogy, the sun represents the intellect. There are emotions your intellect can make you feel: if your intellect tells you that you should feel a certain way, you will feel that way. But there are certain emotions and feelings natural to a person, ingrained in him from birth, that are beyond the power of the intellect; the intellect could never cause such a strong feeling. It is a feeling to the point of *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice), where it does not make sense, like the natural love of a parent for a child, so that the parent would give up his life for the child. That kind of love is not from the intellect; it comes naturally, from the person's essence.

That is called the *middos* of the *ratzon*. They are higher than a reason; it is just the way your nature is, the way Hashem made us: we like things a certain way, we feel very strongly about it, and nothing can change those feelings, "almost nothing." A person always has *bechira* (free choice), and with that he can change everything, but within his nature he will never change.

phrases.en: And these are the emotions within the *ratzon*,
which are higher than a revealed intellect and revealed reason.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן המדות שמצד שכל וטעם נקרא טורי דנהורא,
phrases.en: But the emotions that come about as a result of the intellect and the reason, those are called mountains of light,
because *chachma*, wisdom, the intellect, is called light.

blocks.text: These are the emotions within the *ratzon*, higher than revealed intellect and revealed reason. But the emotions that come as a result of intellect and reason are called *turei d'nehora*, mountains of light, because *chachma*, the intellect, is called light, and when it shines into the *middos* and causes them, the *middos* are called light.

blocks.title: Where the earth protrudes
blocks.text: Why are the *middos* called mountains? A mountain is a place where the Earth protrudes. In the same way, a person's *middos* are where his personality protrudes. The more strongly you feel about something, the more you protrude into the world in that area, and the more effect and interaction you will have with the world around you. A mountain is something that sticks out from you. Something you do not feel strongly about is a little hill, or just a flat plain: you don't care at all.

phrases.he: אבל המדות שברצון נקרא טורי חשוכא,
phrases.en: But the emotions within the *ratzon* are called mountains of darkness,
because these are the emotions that are hidden within the *ratzon*, which are higher than the intellect, and even than a conscious thought.

phrases.he: ושרשם מבחינת חכמה סתימאה הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: And their source is from the hidden *chachma*, not from the revealed *chachma*.
That's called the hidden source of *chachma*.

blocks.text: But the emotions within the *ratzon* are called *turei chashocha*, mountains of darkness, because they are hidden within the *ratzon*, higher than the intellect and even than conscious thought. And their source is the hidden *chachma*, not the revealed *chachma*. The *middos* always come from the *sechel*, and these too come from a *sechel*, but from your subconscious *chachma*, the *chachma* of your *Keser*. That is what was spoken about before with the *mazal*: the source in the *mocha stima'a*. It is called *taalumos chachma* (the hidden depths of wisdom), the hidden source of *chachma*.

phrases.en: This is like the inner reason for a *ratzon*,

phrases.he: שנחלק ממנו ב' קוין חסד וגבורה שברצון כו'
phrases.en: and so from here you have the two lines of *chesed* and *gevura* in the *ratzon*.

blocks.text: This is the *ta'am kamus* (the hidden reason) for the *ratzon*, the inner reason for a will. At this level the *ta'am*, the reason for the will, is a *geshmak*; *ta'am* can also mean a taste. Because a person enjoys things in a certain way, his *ratzon* goes after one thing and not another. That gives the *ratzon* its form, and that is the *chachma*, the intellect, of the *ratzon*. Based on that a person has inherent emotions: he just loves things one way and does not like them another way, not because of a reason but because that is his nature. He likes this and not that, and even if it does not make sense, these supersede anything else, like a person's inherent love for his child, which will supersede all rational considerations.

And from this reason for the *ratzon*, as was said before, from the *sechel*, it already divides up into lines. So from here there are the two lines of *chesed* and *gevura* in the *ratzon*, based on the *sechel*: a *sechel* that leans toward *chesed* and a *sechel* that leans toward *gevura*, whether you like it or you don't like it.

sections.title: Abba and Ima garb the arms: the bribe of the will, and the intellect as its puppet
sections.summary: When *chachma* and *bina* garb the *chesed* and *gevura* of *Arich Anpin*, the intellect only rationalizes a love or bias in the will, like a puppet on the arms. A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise: Rabbi Yishmael, given his own basket of fruit a day early, found his mind arguing for the man. True *sechel* needs the level of the *mazalos*.

phrases.en: And this is why it says

phrases.he: דאבא ואמא מלבישין לזרועות חסד וגבורה דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: that the *Abba* and *Ima*, the *chachma* and *bina*, garb or clothe the arms of *Arich Anpin*, which represents the *chesed* and *gevura* of *Arich Anpin*.

blocks.text: That is why it says that *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina*, garb the arms of *Arich Anpin*, its *chesed* and *gevura*. That is the level where your intellect is based on your essential desires, your *ratzon*: your bias. Let's say you love your child: automatically your intellect is going to look for the good in him, and you are not going to be able to see bad. Or a self-love that covers over your faults. The intellect is now just rationalizing these *middos*.

It is the same when a person feels very strongly about a certain belief, and his intellect tries to explain it and rationalize it. It is not really an intellect; it is really the belief or emotion, which is higher than intellect, and he is just trying to explain it in order to convince. It is not really based on something rational. It is not really open for debate.

You see this with anybody, with missionaries, with political groups, with anybody who feels very strongly about a certain belief and campaigns for it. They will try to convince you rationally, but if you argue and effectively defeat their argument, they still believe in their side, because they believe in it in a way that is higher than the intellect, and they are just trying to convince you. They are not really being rational. "This is not a bad thing or a good thing. This is just a thing. This is the way people work." A person can be like this; a person is always going to be like this some of the time.

sensitivity.reason: Names missionaries and political groups as people who argue from a belief they will not give up even when their argument is defeated.
sensitivity.publishable: You see this in anybody who feels very strongly about a certain belief and campaigns for it. They will try to convince you rationally, but if you argue and effectively defeat their argument, they still believe in their side, because they believe in it in a way that is higher than the intellect; they are just trying to convince you, not really being rational. "This is not a bad thing or a good thing. This is just a thing. This is the way people work." Any person can be like this some of the time.

blocks.text: To really come out with a true *sechel*, you have to go to the first level, where you reach all the way up into the source. That will give you a true understanding. At this level you do not have a true understanding. You will come up with very smart things, but they are based on what you already believe, and it is not the full truth. "It'll be true maybe, but it won't be the full truth."

In holiness too there is this. *Beis Shammai* and *Beis Hillel* would *pasken*, and it was partly based on their source: one leaned toward *chesed* and one leaned toward *gevura*, and so their intellect automatically saw things that way. The idea of the *halacha* is that you have to reach higher than that, all the way into the source, higher than *chesed* and *gevura*, to the *mazalos*, and see where the *hachra'a* is.

There is a whole *maamar*, or a couple of *maamarim*, in *Samech Vav* that explains *eilu v'eilu divrei Elokim chaim* (these and these are the words of the living G-d): how they are both true, but it is not the whole truth. The real truth does not come from *Elokim*; it comes from *Havaya*, which goes higher. That is the level of the *mazalos*, which goes all the way to the essence, and that is where the *halacha* comes from, the ability to decide for one or the other; in this case the *halacha* is like *Beis Hillel*.

Any time a person is in a debate and has a natural leaning toward one side, he just feels that is the right way, and he tries to explain it to you and make you see what he feels, that it is right or that it is wrong. That is usually this level: the intellect is just explaining what the person inherently feels, from his nature. To find the truth you have to go to the higher level, the *mazalos*, where you can see both sides and the inner truth behind both of them, and then you can connect them. "At this level, it's very frustrating to speak to people": if you try to get them to see the other side, or argue the other side, it is not really going to work.

That is why it is like puppets: the intellect becomes a puppet on the arms. The arms go into *chachma* and *bina* and move them the way they want, but it is really just a mask, a front for the *ratzon*. At the level of the *mazalos* you realize that the intellect is also just a front, but at that level you are not biased. You just see the inner truth, and you can bring the intellect out however you want to explain it. There the intellect is even more transparent, but transparent to the intellect behind it, so it comes out as a true *sechel*. That is the level of Torah in general, and of *Chassidus* in particular.

phrases.en: Like we see

phrases.he: שמחמת מדת החסד ואהבה רבה שברצון,
phrases.en: that when a person has an essential desire of *chesed* and *ahava* in their *ratzon*, this infinite love in their *ratzon*,

phrases.he: נמצא שרש לשכל וטעם לזכות ולחסד
phrases.en: this will cause them to have an intellect and a reason for merit and for kindness and for good.

blocks.text: As we see: when a person has an essential desire of *chesed* and *ahava* (love) in his *ratzon*, an infinite love, it gives him an intellect and a reason for merit, for kindness and for good.

phrases.en: Like a bribe: a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise.

phrases.he: שמחמת השוחד שיש לו אהבה ברצון
ממציא טענה ומטעה כח שכלו מחוב לזכות
phrases.en: So this will bring out a *ta'ana*, and it will twist his intellect from guilt to innocence.

blocks.text: That is the idea of a *shochad* (a bribe): a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise. This *chesed*, this love in your *ratzon*, bribes your *sechel* and blinds your intellect to be biased according to it. Whenever you give somebody money, he has an essential desire for money in his *ratzon*, higher than the *sechel*. That desire reaches his *etzem hanefesh* (the essence of the soul) and turns the *sechel* accordingly. It will bring out a *ta'ana* (an argument) and twist his intellect from guilt to innocence. And no matter how holy you are, and even if you do not want it to happen, it is impossible to stop it. Once you connect your *sechel* to a bribe, you are going to be biased.

phrases.he: וכמו ר׳ ישמעאל שלקח כלכלה דפירי, אמר אי בעי טעין הכי כו'

blocks.title: Rabbi Yishmael's basket of fruit
blocks.text:
There are a bunch of stories in *Bava Basra* about bribes, to show you how far they reach. Somebody did a sage some small favor on the day of his court case, and the sage said, "That's already considered a bribe, and I'm not going to judge you."

One of the most extreme is Rabbi Yishmael. He had a sharecropper, and part of the deal was that the sharecropper would bring him a basket of fruit every week, on Friday. This time the man had a court case, so he came up a day early, on Thursday, and since he was coming, he brought the basket with him. The fruit belonged to Rabbi Yishmael, and it was only arriving a day early, but he said, "That's already a bribe, and so I can't judge your case," and he deferred it to another judge. He was there in the *beis midrash* while they judged it, and he said: "The whole time he was speaking, the whole time the case was going on, I was thinking to myself, 'He should've said this. He should've said that.'" His mind was biased, finding ways for the man to win. He told the story to show how strong a bribe is: he found himself inextricably biased toward this person, for such a small favor.

phrases.he: נמצא המדות חסד וגבורה מלובשים בפנימית דאבא ואמא,
phrases.en: So it comes out that the *middos* of *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Keser* go into the *pnimiyus* of the *sechel*, *chachma* and *bina*,

phrases.he: ובחינת אבא ואמא מלבישים אותן מבחוץ
phrases.en: and now *chachma* and *bina* are just like masks or puppets that surround them on the outside.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני בינה לי גבורה
phrases.en: Like it says, "I am *bina*; in me is *gevura*."

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים ודי למבין
phrases.en: Like it says in *Etz Chaim*, and this is enough to understand.

blocks.text: So it comes out that the *middos* of *chesed* and *gevura* of the *Keser* go into the *pnimiyus* (inner part) of the *sechel*, *chachma* and *bina*, and *chachma* and *bina* are just masks or puppets surrounding them on the outside, an external garment covering over the *ratzon*. But it is really a *ratzon*, not really a *sechel*: it is really just this bribe, so to speak.

As it says, "I am *bina*; in me is *gevura*" of *Arich Anpin*. This verse is explained both ways: that *bina* has *gevura* in it, and that *gevura* comes from *bina*. Here he explains it to mean that inside *bina* is hidden the *gevura* of *Arich Anpin*. As it says in *Etz Chaim*, *v'dai l'mevin* (and this is enough for one who understands).

So that is the second level: a person is biased because of an inherent desire that twists the intellect and makes it come up with an intellect according to what he feels.

sections.title: The lowest way: netzach and hod of Arich Anpin, and the yesod of Arich and of Zeir Anpin
sections.summary: Lowest of all, the intellect receives from *netzach* and *hod* of *Arich Anpin*, which carry out *chesed* and *gevura*: the everyday intellect, running on axioms it does not question, though still unlimited because it serves the will. The *yesod* of *Arich Anpin* is the abundant good, a cedar valued for itself; the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* is small, a palm kept for its fruit, down to the hyssop in the wall.

phrases.en: And then as the light descends lower,

phrases.he: אין מוחין דחכמה ובינה דאצילות מקבלים רק מבחינת נצח והוד דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: there's an even lower level, where the intellect only receives from the *netzach* and *hod* of *Arich Anpin*,

phrases.he: שהוא הבאת השפע דחסד וגבורה למטה
phrases.en: which *netzach* and *hod* just bring out the *chesed* and *gevura* to actuality; they're bringing it down.

phrases.he: כמו נצח והוד שנקרא מאזני צדק בכמה מקומות,
phrases.en: Like *netzach* and *hod*, which are called the scales of justice; on every level they're called the scales of justice.

phrases.he: גם למטה במדות שמצד אור השכל
phrases.en: This is true also in the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*, which are under the *sechel*.

blocks.text: As the light descends lower, there is an even lower level, where the intellect receives only from the *netzach* and *hod* (victory and acknowledgement) of *Arich Anpin*. *Netzach* and *hod* just bring *chesed* and *gevura* out to actuality, bringing them down. They are called *moznei tzedek*, the scales of justice, on every level: this is true also in the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance), which are under the *sechel*. Whether the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin* or of *Arich Anpin*, *netzach* and *hod* always bring the flow down, and that is the scales of justice.

Once you have figured out what is good and what is bad, you come to a particular situation and have to figure out the best way to bring this law, this ruling, to actuality. You weigh what would be just in this situation, like the sentence as opposed to the verdict, to figure out how to actually carry out the law. What should we do to the person? Should we punish him? Should we reward him? How should we punish him, how should we reward him? You weigh: should I give, or should I hold back?

phrases.he: רק במדות שברצון שנקרא אריכות דאנפין,
phrases.en: The only difference is that when it's in the *middos* of the *ratzon*, the *middos* of *Keser*, there it's called *Arich Anpin*, it's called a big face.
At that level, *netzach* and *hod* are not limited,
just like the *ratzon* itself,
which is not limited.

phrases.he: על כן גם בחינת נצח והוד

phrases.en: They're also unlimited.

blocks.text: The only difference is that in the *middos* of the *ratzon*, the *middos* of *Keser*, it is called *Arich Anpin*, a big face: mature, infinite *middos*. At that level *netzach* and *hod* are not limited; none of the *middos* there are limited, just like the *ratzon* itself, the will of *Arich Anpin*, which is infinite. "So, in *Arich Anpin*, you don't want a good job, you want infinite money. You don't want a nice house, you want a huge palace." Everything there is without end. So the emotions of *Chagas* there, the love and the fear, are infinite, essential *middos*, and so are the *netzach* and *hod*, and the *yesod*: the *Nehi* there is also like that.

So *netzach* and *hod* there are also unlimited. Because of a person's essential love for his family, he will want to work to provide them with food, clothing, shelter and all their needs. Since it comes from his essential desire, it comes out as an essential *netzach* and *hod* as well: the application, "because I love my family, I have to provide for them," is also essential, and it will never stop.

When the intellect receives from this *netzach* and *hod*, it is already a normal intellect, the regular way your intellect works. On a regular day you are not thinking about the inner truth behind things, which would be the *mazalos*, going all the way up to the *Chabad* and to the *etzem* that is higher than the *Chabad*, the *Keser*. And you are not thinking about your inner beliefs, values and morals, which would be the *Chagas*. You are just thinking about how to do your day-to-day things, based on your beliefs, your worldview, your nature, your feelings and your morals, which are already set; now you are just applying them. The *netzach* and *hod* of it is that I have to go to work: you figure out how to drive to work, and once you get there how to do your job, and how to get your groceries, and just do your day-to-day stuff.

That is already a regular intellect. In a way it is kind of honest, because you are not so partial; but on the other hand you are not looking into the truth of things at all. You are assuming this whole system, all these axioms, and working from there. You already assume that you want to go to work, that you love your family, that this is the right thing to do, and that's it; you are not questioning any of it. To really get to the truth of an idea, you have to question all the way back to the original axioms, see whether they are true, and build from there. If you do not dig into the source, you will never really find the truth of an idea. But once it is all set up, the intellect just runs on autopilot.

phrases.en: As it's known, that when it says, "Remember your abundant goodness,"
that's the idea of *yesod* of *Arich Anpin*.
And see also that it says, "Your great goodness," and the like.

phrases.he: וכן אם יגאלך טוב, ורב טוב לבית ישראל וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: It says, if you will bestow goodness, and abundant goodness to the House of Israel.

blocks.text: As is known, *zecher rav tuvcha*, "Remember Your abundant goodness," is the *yesod* of *Arich Anpin*. *Tov* (good) represents *yesod*, as will be explained later, and "Your great goodness", infinite good, is called *rav tuvcha*: the *yesod* of *Arich Anpin*. That is the level where G-d connects to us in an infinite way, and so He always wants to give to us, no matter what. So too "Your great goodness" and the like, and "if you will bestow goodness, and abundant goodness to the House of Israel." Here you see two: the regular *tov*, which is of *Zeir Anpin*, and the *rav tov*, which is of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בחינת יסוד זעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: But the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*:
those are the emotions that come only based on a reason; they're coming out from the intellect.
Those are very small, very immature.

blocks.text: But the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* is the *middos* born from *bina*, emotions that come only from a reason, out of the intellect, and they are very small, very immature. You are connected to the thing only for a reason, and as soon as the reason goes away, you won't do it anymore.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין צדיק כתמר, שזהו בחינת יסוד זעיר אנפין
כארז בלבנון ישגה, בבחינת אין סוף,
שהוא ביסוד עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין
phrases.en: That's the *yesod* of *Atik* and *Arich*.

blocks.text: As it is explained elsewhere about *tzaddik katamar yifrach, k'erez balevanon yisgeh*, the *tzaddik* will flourish like a palm, he will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon. The palm is the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*; the cedar in Lebanon is the infinite, the *yesod* of *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*. (In reading, he says the text there is supposed to read *Ein Sof*.) A *tzaddik* represents *yesod*, as will also be explained later, and he starts out growing like a date palm, and eventually he becomes like a cedar.

blocks.title: The date palm
blocks.text: What is a date palm? The purpose of the tree is the fruit. As soon as it stops giving fruit the tree is worthless; it is not good wood or anything, mostly a useless tree. Its main purpose is just the fruit. That is the level where a person is doing something, growing and working, but only for a reason. He is connected to it only because of the fruit, and his whole purpose is the fruit, "like a kid that's doing, you know, learning for candy," or doing something for a reward. Those are the small *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*.

blocks.title: The cedar
blocks.text: The *yesod* of *Arich Anpin* is doing it with an inherent integrity, just because you want to do it, and that is the cedar. A cedar has no fruit, but the tree itself is valuable, its wood is valuable. You do it because the thing itself is valuable, not because of what it will bring you; you appreciate that this itself is what you want to do. You do a good deed for somebody, or help somebody, because it is the right thing to do, not for a reward. The same with Torah and *mitzvos*: if you do them because you want to connect to Hashem, *s'char mitzva mitzva* (the reward of a *mitzva* is the *mitzva*). Being able to connect to Hashem is the reward, and you do not need some separate reward, *Olam Haba* or *Gan Eden* or money or blessings. That is the cedar: the fruit is the thing itself.

And it is in Lebanon, *Levanon*, which is *lamed-beis nun*: the source of *chachma* and *bina*, the thirty-two paths of *chachma* and the fiftieth gate of *bina*, where they reach all the way up to the *etzem*, as opposed to just the external things that come out of it. When you appreciate the thing itself, that is a cedar in Lebanon.

phrases.en: And similarly, like it says about *Shlomo HaMelech*,

phrases.he: וידבר מן הארז אשר בלבנון עד האזוב,
phrases.en: he spoke about the cedar tree that's in Lebanon, all the way to the weed that grows out of the wall,

phrases.he: בחינת קטנות יסוד זעיר אנפין במלכות, שנקרא קיר כו'

blocks.text: So too what it says about *Shlomo HaMelech*, King Solomon, the wisest man: he spoke about everything, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop in the wall. He explained everything, the plants and the animals; and when he spoke about the plants, he spoke about everything from the cedar tree in Lebanon all the way to the weed that grows out of the wall, from the greatest tree to the smallest little weed. He explained the actual plants, but it also means he explained *yesod*, which is like a plant: the ground is like *Malchus*, and the tree grows out of it and stays connected to it, like the *middos* at the level of *yesod*, where they connect to *Malchus*.

The cedar in Lebanon, as explained, is the *yesod* of *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, and he explained all the way down to the smallest *yesod*, the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, which grows out of *Malchus*, called the *kir*, the wall. A wall is like *Malchus* because it is *batel* (nullified), completely; it is just an inanimate thing. "And that's like, you know, in the *Kosel*, they have weeds growing out of the cracks there." That is a weed growing out of the wall.

phrases.he: (וכידוע בכוונות דאמן יהא שמיא רבא מברך
phrases.en: And this is the idea when we *daven* and we say *Amen yehei shmei rabba mevarach*: what are we saying?
*Shmei*, your name, has the same *gematria* as *ratzon*, desire.

phrases.he: ושמו הגדול בבחינת יסוד ומלכות דאריך
phrases.en: *Shmei rabba*, your great name, the big name: that's the *yesod* and the *Malchus* of *Arich Anpin*.

phrases.he: שיהיה מבורך באבא ואמא וזעיר אנפין ונוקבא כו'
phrases.en: We're saying that it should be drawn down into the *sechel*, the *Abba* and *Ima*, and then *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*.
That the right should overpower the left.

phrases.he: וכמו ובטובך הגדול ישוב כו' ודי למבין)
phrases.en: Like we say, "In Your abundant goodness return us."

blocks.text: As is known in the *kavanos* (the mystical intentions) of *Amen yehei shmei rabba mevarach*: when we *daven* (pray) and say it, what are we saying? We say *Amen*, may Your great name be blessed. What is Your name? *Shmei*, Your name, has the same *gematria* (numerical value) as *ratzon*, desire. *Shmei rabba*, Your great name, the big name, is the *yesod* and the *Malchus* of *Arich Anpin*. The *Malchus* is the *shem* (name), and when it is connected to *Zeir Anpin* through *yesod*, that is called *shmei*, Your name. We are saying that it should be drawn down into the *sechel*, *Abba* and *Ima*, and then *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*: that Hashem's great name should be brought out, *l'agbara yemina al smala*, the right should overpower the left. We are asking that Hashem's essential connection to the Jews be brought out and revealed, so that He will have mercy on us. As we say, "In Your abundant goodness return us," *v'dai l'mevin*.

The main idea of this is really that we are asking for *Moshiach*. As was explained before, he thinks, *shmei rabba* means all the way up to the original *ratzon*, the *ratzon kadum* (the primordial will), which is the will for *Moshiach*. Here he stresses that it is brought out into *Abba* and *Ima* and *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*: when the *middos* are according to the essential *ratzon*, it will always be the same. Hashem has an essential connection to us, and so whether we deserve it or not, Hashem will always give us good. So this is the lowest level of the intellect, where it receives from the *ratzon*, but even there it is always according to the *ratzon*.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the three ways *Abba* and *Ima* receive from *Arich Anpin*, and which is highest?

What are the *mazalos* in the brain, and why do the first six bring pleasure and the last six intellect?
